newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finmin Thanong sees single-digit inflation.
newsitem.headline: Thai finmin Thanong sees single-digit inflation.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya voiced confidence on Tuesday that inflation would not surge into double digits in 1997 despite the baht losing 15-20 percent of its value since last week.
Thanong told reporters: "Inflation does not warrant concern. It is expected to start easing in 1998 and will not be in double digits (this year)."
The minister said he expected the Thai consumer price index to rise about 6.0 percent year-on-year in the next one to two months, against 4.4 percent in June and 5.9 percent in the whole 1996.
Thanong said food prices have eased this month in line with slower consumer spending and tightened liquidity in the money market.

He said the Thai government is setting aside 20 billion baht for lending to private business affected by its decision to let the baht loose on a managed float last week. The minister said borrowers of the loan would be charged a concessional 8.0 percent interest rate. He did not elaborate.
